data.title: Worldline slumps as FT report raises questions over cash-flow practices
data.description:
Worldline shares fell around 16% on Friday, having touched a record low earlier in the session, after the Financial Times reported that the payment group had bolstered its cash flow by delaying supplier payments and securing advance payments from customers.

The report, which cited documents seen by the FT and three people familiar with the company, said Worldline repeatedly pushed back payments to suppliers, while requesting cash advances from clients ahead of reporting periods, practices allegedly used until 2023 when its stock suffered a sharp selloff.

In a statement responding to the allegations, Worldline said its accounts had been systematically reviewed by its audit committee and reiterated its annual guidance.

data.title: Sri Lankan shares log worst week in six months after surprise central bank rate hike
data.description:
Sri Lankan shares closed lower on Friday, dragged down by broad-based losses across sectors after the central bank raised its key policy rate, marking their worst week since mid-May.

Here are some details:

  • The CSE All Share index settled 0.8% lower at 21,369.72, shedding 2.97% over a week, that snapped its three-week winning streak

  • Sri Lanka's central bank raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points in a surprise move on Friday, citing higher-than-expected inflation pressures caused by volatile global energy prices

  • RENUKA HOTELS and ALPHA FIRE were the top percentage losers on the CSE All Share index, falling 8.98% and 6.85%, respectively.

  • Trading volume on the CSE All Share index rose to 121.8 million shares from 53.8 million in the previous session.

  • The equity market's turnover rose to 2.33 billion Sri Lankan rupees ($7.01 million) from 1.73 billion rupees in the previous session, according to exchange data.

  • Foreign investors were net sellers, offloading stocks worth 52.6 million rupees, while domestic investors were net buyers, purchasing shares worth 2.32 billion rupees, the data showed.

data.title: Erasca Reports ERAS-0015 Response Data, Accelerates Pancreatic Cancer Phase 3
data.description:
Erasca reported encouraging interim ERAS-0015 activity across RAS-mutant cancers and moved its planned first-line pancreatic cancer Phase 3 trial to the first half of 2027.

Key Highlights:

  • ERAS-0015 showed a 44% confirmed response rate in second-line-or-later KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer patients at 32 mg once daily (N=25).
  • Confirmed response rates were 58% in KRAS G12X lung cancer across 16–32 mg doses (N=12) and 75% in biliary tract cancer at 32 mg (N=4).
  • Monotherapy was generally well tolerated at active doses; no dose discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events occurred at 32 mg.
  • Early combination findings supported further development, while preliminary ERAS-4001 data supported its potential combination with ERAS-0015; a combination dose-escalation trial is planned for 2027.

to be implemented by means of a Scheme of Arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006

UPDATE ON SATISFACTION OF CONDITIONS AND TIMETABLE

On 5 September 2026, the Spire Directors and Bidco Board announced that they had reached agreement on the terms of a recommended final* cash offer, pursuant to which Bidco will acquire the entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital of Spire that the Consortium does not already own (the “Acquisition”). The Acquisition is intended to be effected by means of a Court approved scheme of arrangement under Part 26 of the Companies Act 2006 (the “Scheme”). Full details of the Scheme are set out in the scheme document published on 29 September 2026 (the “Scheme Document”).

As announced by Spire on 30 October 2026, the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Scheme Shareholders at the Court Meeting held on 30 October 2026 and the Resolution relating to the implementation of the Scheme was approved by the requisite majority of Spire Shareholders at the General Meeting also held on 30 October 2026.

* The financial terms of the Cash Offer and the Alternative Offer are final. Bidco may not revise the Cash Offer or the Alternative Offer other than in exceptional circumstances and only with the prior consent of the Panel. Bidco reserves the right to elect to implement the Acquisition by way of a Takeover Offer as an alternative to the Scheme, subject to obtaining the consent of the Panel and subject to the terms of the Co-operation Agreement.

Satisfaction of FCA Regulatory Condition

Spire and Bidco are pleased to confirm that, on 19 November 2026, the FCA Regulatory Condition set out in paragraph 3(a) of Part A of Part III of the Scheme Document was satisfied.

Completion of the Acquisition remains subject to the satisfaction (or, where applicable, waiver) of the remaining Conditions set out in the Scheme Document, including the sanction of the Scheme by the Court at the Court Hearing and the delivery of a copy of the Court Order to the Registrar of Companies.

Next steps and timetable

An updated expected timetable of remaining principal events for the implementation of the Scheme is set out below. Spire and Bidco confirm that the Court Hearing has been scheduled to be held on 3 December 2026. Details of the Court Hearing will be available on the Business and Property Division Rolls Building Daily Cause List at www.court-tribunal-hearings.service.gov.uk on the day before the Court Hearing.

Subject to the Scheme receiving the sanction of the Court at the Court Hearing, the Effective Date for the Acquisition is expected to be 7 December 2026. The last day of dealings in, and for registration of transfers of, Spire Shares on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange is expected to be on 4 December 2026, with all dealings in Spire Shares being suspended by 7.30 a.m. on 7 December 2026. It is also expected that the admission to trading of Spire Shares on the Main Market and listing of Spire Shares on the Official List will each be cancelled by 8.00 a.m. on 8 December 2026.

These dates and times are based on Spire’s and Bidco’s current expectations and are subject to change. If any of the dates and/or times in the expected timetable change, the revised dates and/or times will be notified to Spire Shareholders by announcement through a Regulatory Information Service, with such announcement being made available on Spire’s website at www.investors.spirehealthcare.com and Bidco’s website at www.toscafund.com.

Elections for the Alternative Offer

The Election Return Time, being the latest time for delivering the Form of Election (for certificated holders) or settlement of TTE Instructions (for CREST holders) in respect of the Alternative Offer, will be 1.00 p.m. on 2 December 2026, being the Business Day prior to the Court Hearing.

The KYC Return Time, being the latest time for submitting KYC Information in respect of the Alternative Offer in a form satisfactory to Bidco, will be 1.00 p.m. on 30 November 2026, being the third Business Day prior to the Court Hearing.

data.title: Dollar set for fourth weekly gain, supported by Fed tightening expectations, AI-driven haven bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar index near strongest since early April 2025
  • Markets debating size, not likelihood, of December Fed hike
  • Yen firms after Japanese core inflation hits 2.2%

By Sophie Kiderlin

The dollar was steady on Friday and was on track to rise for the fourth straight week as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening underpinned the US currency and jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, around its strongest since early April 2025. The weeks-long rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

The dollar was also supported by a reduced appetite for risk, with a multitude of AI-related concerns weighing on global stocks. Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session EURONEXT:IACWI on Friday, the longest losing streak since 2023.

Chris Turner, global head of markets at ING, said that while there is only a weak case for another steep correction in equities, "there is no reason for the Fed to drop its hawkish rhetoric anytime soon."

He pointed to next week's US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, a key inflation gauge for the Fed, which Turner said will likely confirm that the Fed needs to act.

"For FX, that means a continued strong dollar and continued pressure on popular carry trades," he said.

In FX carry trades, investors borrow in low-yielding currencies, such as the Japanese yen and Swiss franc, to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets elsewhere, often in emerging markets.

Adding to the hawkish-leaning narrative, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own.

"The debate now is not really about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, but how much it will raise rates by," Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said.

"We still think 25 basis points is more likely," Kong added. "If they really want to quicken the pace of tightening, I think they will prefer to increase rates by 25 bps in consecutive meetings rather than deliver a bigger-than-usual hike."

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3105, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0961.

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

The yen firmed 0.6% against the dollar to 158.78 and is set to close the week with a small gain after three weeks of losses that had dragged the currency to near the key 160 level.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

ING's Turner also noted that a carry trade unwind should be a slight positive for the yen.

data.title: White House Reportedly Replaces Cyber Director Sean Cairncross Amid Widespread US Tech Outages
data.description:
Key points:
  • Kirsten Davies, a former technology and cybersecurity executive at Unilever, Estée Lauder and Hewlett Packard, will serve as acting cyber director.
  • Cairncross was confirmed by the Senate in August 2025 and previously led the Millennium Challenge Corporation.
  • The White House said it sees “no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor” behind the recent tech outages.

The White House has reportedly replaced National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, following a series of major technology outages across the U.S.

Cairncross was no longer with the administration, Bloomberg reported, citing a White House official. A person familiar with the matter told the publication that he had been dismissed and Davies would replace him in an acting capacity.

A permanent national cyber director must first be nominated by the president and then confirmed by the Senate.

Cairncross, who was confirmed by the Senate in August 2025, previously served as a senior adviser to the White House chief of staff during Trump's first term and led the Millennium Challenge Corporation, Bloomberg reported.

White House Cyber Leadership Change

President Donald Trump's chief of staff, Stephen Miller, pushed for Cairncross's removal, two White House officials told Axios, with one official saying he “lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job.”

Davies previously held technology and cybersecurity roles at Unilever, Estée Lauder and Hewlett Packard, according to Bloomberg. Davies thanked Trump and Miller for their confidence in her.

“Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come …but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future. Under President Trump’s leadership, we will have a more secure, resilient, and supercharged technological future, she wrote on X.

Tech Outages Affect Aviation, Microsoft, Government Systems

The leadership change comes after several major technology disruptions, including a nationwide aviation ground stop, a worldwide Microsoft (MSFT) Outlook outage and a reported blackout of the National Security Agency's classified communications network.

The White House said Wednesday, “The Trump Administration sees no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity, or malign actor behind the recent tech outages.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio also told reporters in Manila on Wednesday that the U.S. had no indication or evidence that the disruptions were connected or resulted from hostile acts, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: India meets ethanol blending goal as corn, rice boost supplies, industry body data shows
data.description:
India achieved its target of blending 20% ethanol with petrol in the 2025/26 supply year, as higher production of the biofuel from corn and rice lifted the average blending rate, an industry body said on Friday.

The average blending rate reached 19.99%, up from 19.24% a year earlier, with 11.34 billion litres of ethanol blended with petrol during the year ended October 31, the All India Distillers' Association said.

Corn-based ethanol accounted for a record 46% of total supplies, lifting the share of grain-based ethanol to 76%. Sugarcane-based feedstocks made up the remaining 24%, the association said.

However, ethanol blending could fall short of the government's 20% target in the supply year that began this month, industry insiders said, with the lowest monsoon rainfall in more than a decade threatening corn and sugarcane crops and forcing New Delhi to prioritise food security over ethanol production.

data.title: Deutsche Bank leaks add spice to succession debate
data.description:
By Neil Unmack

A 15-mln-document dump outlines how the €56 bln bank accidentally forwarded Donald Trump’s tax return, and other missteps. It’s mostly old news. But Deutsche's shares have dipped, and it raises the question of what happens after CEO Christian Sewing's mandate ends in 2029.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow @Unmack1 on X

CONTEXT NEWS

The Financial Times this week published a series of articles based on leaks of internal documents at Deutsche Bank. The leaks, which were reviewed by over 200 journalists from publications including Der Spiegel and Le Monde, include revelations that Deutsche accidentally forwarded Donald Trump’s tax return to a third party, without disclosing it had done so.

The documents also list about $582 million in transactions linked to Jeffery Epstein, which were flagged internally as suspicious. Internal emails indicate that senior executives approved Epstein as a client despite his conviction, and kept his accounts open even after warnings about the activities of Ghislaine Maxwell, his former girlfriend and associate.

“The matters which are in focus of the media reports date back many years and in some cases as much as two decades," Deutsche said in a statement. “Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators.”

Deutsche said it had invested €7 billion in its controls between 2019 and 2025, adding that “we are a different, stronger and safer bank today”.

Deutsche Bank shares were trading at €29 as of 0930 GMT on November 20, down over 10% since the start of the week.

data.title: The Logistics Report: Union Pacific CEO Apologizes as March Remark Fuels Opposition to Merger — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
By Mark R. Long

Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena apologized for saying at a conference in March that he would raise rates for customers who don't support the merger of his railroad with Norfolk Southern.

"If I had to do it again, I wouldn't have said it," Vena said Thursday during a panel at the RailTrends conference in New York.

The Wall Street Journal's Esther Fung writes that Vena is trying to gather support for the $72 billion deal, which would create the first transcontinental U.S. railroad with a single operator. Proponents say the deal would cut shipping times and take less-efficient trucks off highways. Opponents, however, argue that competition will decrease and shippers will be worse off with fewer rail options.

In March, Vena said he would raise rates for shippers who don't support the merger, "to teach you a lesson." Vena's comments were mentioned or alluded to in several comments that opponents of the merger filed with the Surface Transportation Board, which is reviewing the deal, TrainsPRO reports.

On Thursday, Vena repeated that (Union Pacific) doesn't retaliate against customers and that the railroad was open to discussions with concerned shippers.

"It was my attempt at humor. I made a mistake."Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena

Retail

Walmart said its quarterly revenue rose 5.2%, with sales and profit from e-commerce, advertising and other newer businesses growing while in-store sales slid. The retail giant raised its financial guidance for the full year, and said comparable sales from stores and digital channels grew 2.9%, the WSJ's Sarah Nassauer writes.

Its most recent U.S. sales were helped by market-share gains in its food business, but hurt by pricing regulation in its pharmacy business. The retailer's global e-commerce sales grew by 17% and 23% in the U.S. Its U.S. advertising business was up 37%. E-commerce now accounts for around a quarter of (Walmart's) total sales.

Walmart also said it was using its online-ordering infrastructure to make more fast-food deliveries along with groceries and other products. Frontier Minerals, a consortium that includes two Indiana-based companies-American Resources Corp. and ReElement Technologies-as well as Idaho-based Bunker Hill Mining Group, beat out rivals for the license after a more than six-month competition. Two Chinese companies withdrew before the final bids, with no public explanation.

data.title: AI Stocks Tumble Across the Globe as Slowdown Fears Mount
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Artificial intelligence stocks fell across the globe as sentiment around the AI trade deteriorated further, despite Anthropic's record-breaking IPO Thursday.

Nasdaq futures were 1.3% lower as the index headed toward its worst one-week performance since President Trump's April 2025 imposition of sweeping tariffs. Chip makers and cloud-computing stocks sold off. Intel and Micron Technology fell 4.5% and 5.2% premarket, respectively, while Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 6.2%, extending a sharp fall from the last session following a short-seller report into the company published Thursday. Stocks that benefit from the build-out in AI suffered too, with data center power-supplier Caterpillar down 2.5% premarket.

Tech giants that served as havens in previous AI wobbles provided no safety premarket, with Meta Platforms and Microsoft both falling more than 1%.

So-called Animal spirits are taking over the market, XTB's Kathleen Brooks said. Multiple fears are weighing on investors' outlook, the research director said, including worries about high financing costs, excessive AI spending and legislation that could hurt the technology in the U.S.

Combined, those factors threaten a pullback in the AI build-out that could lead to lower revenues for related companies.

Asian stocks were hit hard Friday. South Korean memory-chip makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell 7% and 5.9%, respectively. In Japan, SoftBank Group--a major backer of OpenAI--fell 14.5%.

Europe's most valuable company, Dutch supplier of chip-making equipment ASML, fell close to 6%, putting it on track to lose around 28 billion euros of market value ($30.71 billion). A gauge of the continent's tech sector fell 3.6%.

Anthropic itself was down more than 6.5% premarket to trade around $90.80 a share. Adding to pressure on the stock was news, first reported by Bloomberg, that Apple is developing a new autonomous AI agent. The consumer-focused product could offer fresh competition to Anthropic's models.

Analysts are also concerned that Anthropic's revenue growth won't be enough to significantly outpace its spending commitments. The model maker has spending commitments totaling $900.9 billion, around half of which are due over the next five years, according to its IPO filing with the SEC.

"We are concerned about Anthropic's revenue growth," Seaport Research senior analyst Jay Goldberg wrote in a note. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years."

Investors are ditching AI stocks over fears that the sector's spending boom has passed its peak "in spite of a lack of any compelling evidence as yet of any such development on the ground," Jefferies' global head of equity strategy, Christopher Wood, said.

Driving the fear are concerns that Nvidia will step back from its role as financier-in-chief for the wider AI ecosystem, Wood said. In particular, investors worry Nvidia will pull its backing of chip-hungry cloud-computing startups, Wood said.

"This suggests a real risk that the most speculative part of the demand for compute will disappear which should lower compute prices for others."
